cues.en: These early telescopes relied on a curved piece of glass a bit like this one I'm holding here that take distant starlight and bend it towards a focus point. Now that bending is caused by refraction.
cues.zh: 这些早期望远镜依赖一块弧形玻璃，有点像我手里拿的这块，它把远处的星光折射到一个焦点上。这种折射是由折射现象引起的。

cues.en: That's what happens when light passes from one medium like air into a denser medium like glass,
cues.zh: 当光线从空气这样的介质进入玻璃这样更密集的介质时就会发生这种情况，

cues.en: And two, the very fact that this lens is larger physically than my eye means it also collects more light and thus we get amplification.
cues.zh: 第二，这块透镜在物理尺寸上比我的眼睛更大，这意味着它也能收集更多光线，从而实现了增强。

cues.en: And so you have a ludicrous telescope,
cues.zh: 于是你拥有了一架荒谬绝伦的望远镜，

cues.en: one so powerful that it could provide an image like this of an Earth sized planet from a 100 light years away.
cues.zh: 它威力巨大，能拍出这样的画面：在100光年外拍摄一颗地球大小的行星。

cues.en: It was Italian physicist Claudio Maccone who proposed a mission to the European Space Agency in 1993
cues.zh: 正是意大利物理学家克劳迪奥·马科内（Claudio Maccone）在1993年向欧洲空间局提出了一项任务，

cues.en: to exploit this lens called focal.
cues.zh: 利用这种被称为“太阳引力透镜”的透镜。

cues.en: Unfortunately, the mission did not progress with critics citing that the distance of 550
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，这项任务并未推进，批评者认为550

cues.en: a u is simply too far. It's more than three and a half times further out than our most distant probes are right now. Moreover, you can only really look at what is directly behind the sun at any one time and because this thing is so far out,
cues.zh: 个天文单位的距离实在是太远了。它比我们目前最远的探测器还要远三倍半以上。此外，你在任何特定时间基本上只能观测到太阳正后方的东西，而且因为这东西距离太远，

cues.en: its orbital period around the sun is very slow and thus you're pretty limited in what you can look at. Finally, the corona of the sun is literally a hot mess to deal with poking out of the solar disk in random ways as anyone who's witnessed a solar eclipse can attest to. And so focal has never really been taken that seriously by NASA or any other space agency.
cues.zh: 它绕太阳的轨道周期非常慢，因此你能观测的目标非常受限。最后，太阳的日冕处理起来简直是一团乱麻，它以各种随机的方式从太阳盘面突出来，任何见过日食的人都能作证。因此，focal 任务从未真正被 NASA 或任何其他航天机构认真对待过。

cues.en: It doesn't feature anyone's long term planning or future roadmaps
cues.zh: 它没有出现在任何人的长期规划或未来路线图中。

cues.en: And so we turn back to glass,
cues.zh: 所以我们转回玻璃，

cues.en: we turn back to mirrors, we turn back to segmented designs,
cues.zh: 我们转回镜子，我们转回分块式设计，

cues.en: and we limit ourselves to more
cues.zh: 而我们自己则局限于更加

cues.en: modest science,
cues.zh: 温和的科学，

cues.en: more realistic goals,
cues.zh: 更加现实的目标，

cues.en: more proven technologies.
cues.zh: 更加成熟的技术。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 好吧，

cues.en: bollocks to that. Okay. So fine, maybe the sun is out of our current reach, but the concept is brilliant.
cues.zh: 去他的吧。好吧，没关系，也许太阳超出了我们目前的触及范围，但这个概念太棒了。

cues.en: What if we could replace the sun with a different natural lens,
cues.zh: 如果我们能用另一种天然透镜取代太阳呢？

cues.en: a nearby astronomical object which could serve as an intermediate stepping stone for us to hone our lensing skills and yet at the same time achieve
cues.zh: 一个附近的天体，可以充当中间的跳板，让我们逐步磨练引力透镜技术，同时实现

cues.en: colossal
cues.zh: 巨大的

cues.en: lensing capabilities,
cues.zh: 引力透镜能力，

cues.en: something closer
cues.zh: 选择一个离我们

cues.en: to home.
cues.zh: 更近的天体。

cues.en: At first, the idea of using the earth as a natural lens
cues.zh: 乍一看，把地球当作天然透镜的想法

cues.en: seems ridiculous.
cues.zh: 似乎很荒谬。

cues.en: After all, the earth is 300,000
cues.zh: 毕竟，地球的质量比太阳小30万

cues.en: times less massive than the sun and so Einstein's theory tells us that it should barely deflect light at all.
cues.zh: 倍，因此，根据爱因斯坦的理论，它几乎无法使光线发生偏转。

cues.en: But gravity
cues.zh: 但在光线弯曲这件事上，

cues.en: is not the only game in town when it comes to bending light. Thirteen years ago,
cues.zh: 起作用的并不只有引力。十三年前，

cues.en: I wrote this,
cues.zh: 我写下了这篇论文，

cues.en: the green flash and the green ring.
cues.zh: 主题是绿闪和绿环现象。

cues.en: This is my master's
cues.zh: 这是我在

cues.en: thesis during my time at Cambridge University.
cues.zh: 剑桥大学求学期间的硕士

cues.en: It was a necessary part of my degree to undertake some research and so I chose a subject
cues.zh: 毕业论文。根据学位要求，我必须开展一些研究，于是我选择了一个

cues.en: that was as close to planets as I could find. It was doctor Peter Duffett Smith, my adviser, who offered me a project to try and explain the green flash phenomenon.
cues.zh: 尽可能贴近行星领域的课题。我的导师 Peter Duffett Smith 博士给我提供了一个项目，让我尝试解释绿闪现象。

cues.en: Now this is a well known effect and I bet many of you have even seen it. So I think he offered this project every year. It wasn't supposed to lead to a natural publication or something, but rather just give a taste of what research was like. When the Sun is about to set it's actually already half a degree below the horizon,
cues.zh: 这是一种广为人知的现象，我敢说你们很多人都亲眼见过。我想，他每年都会提供这个课题。这个项目本来也没打算发表成正式论文什么的，只是想让学生体验一下科研是什么样的。当太阳即将落山时，实际上它已经位于地平线以下半度了，

cues.en: but light is bent through the atmosphere
cues.zh: 但光线穿过大气层时会发生偏折，

cues.en: due to refraction.
cues.zh: 这是由折射造成的。

cues.en: Refraction which is remember the very same effect that was used in the oldest telescope designs.
cues.zh: 折射其实就是古老望远镜设计中采用的同一种光学效应。

cues.en: Now blue light refracts more than green and green light more than red and so in principle,
cues.zh: 现在，蓝光的折射率大于绿光，绿光的折射率又大于红光，因此按理说，

cues.en: the very last bit of light that you see coming off the sun should be blue light.
cues.zh: 你从太阳上看到的最后一缕光应该是蓝光。

cues.en: But because of scattering in the earth's atmosphere, blue light is essentially attenuated
cues.zh: 但由于地球大气层的散射，蓝光基本上被完全

cues.en: completely
cues.zh: 衰减了，

cues.en: and thus the only little bit of light that you have a chance of seeing is the green, hence the name green flash.
cues.zh: 因此你唯一有机会看到的一点光就是绿光，这就是“绿闪”名字的由来。

cues.en: So I went ahead and came up with a simple model to describe the atmosphere, wrote some software for doing the simulations,
cues.zh: 于是我着手建立了一个描述大气层的简单模型，编写了一些用于模拟的软件，

cues.en: and I calculated the deflection of light and the scattering effects. As a personal side note, I have to say this was a formative experience for me. I got a real kick out of doing some research like this and it gave me confidence that yeah, could problem solve, I could do research and maybe this could be a career for me after I graduate. But towards the final section of my thesis, I also realized that one could potentially see a green flash from space.
cues.zh: 并计算了光的偏折和散射效应。作为个人的题外话，我必须说这对我是一次具有决定意义的经历。进行这样的研究让我感到非常兴奋，它给了我信心，让我觉得没错，我能解决问题，我能做研究，也许这可以成为我毕业后的职业发展方向。但在论文的最后一部分，我也意识到人们实际上有可能从太空中看到绿闪。

cues.en: In fact, if the sun were directly behind the earth and you were located as I calculated it back then, two thirds the distance between the earth and the moon, then you could see a green ring around the earth. I even hacked together this visualization
cues.zh: 事实上，如果太阳正好在地球正后方，而你的位置正如我当年计算的那样——位于地月距离的三分之二处，那么你就能看到围绕地球的一圈绿色光环。我甚至用Photoshop和一张日食的照片，拼凑出了

cues.en: of what this green ring might even look like by using photoshop and an image of a solar eclipse.
cues.zh: 这个绿色光环可能呈现样子的可视化图像。

cues.en: But I mean this was an intellectual curiosity
cues.zh: 但这在当时只是出于知识上的好奇

cues.en: and you know my advisors have broadly agreed with that.
cues.zh: 我的导师们也大体上认同这一点。

cues.en: But I remember one thing that he said to me was that he'd never seen anybody approach the problem quite in this way before after a years of offering this project
cues.zh: 但我记得他对我说过一件事：在他多年提供这个项目的过程中，他从未见过有人用这种方式来处理这个问题

cues.en: and something about that stuck with me. And so I think in the back of my mind, I always thought maybe maybe one day
cues.zh: 这一点让我一直记在心里。所以我想，在内心深处，我一直觉得也许有一天

cues.en: I should turn back to this and investigate it further, see if there was anything to this. Many years later during my time at Harvard University as a Sagan postdoc,
cues.zh: 我应该回过头来研究这个，看看这里面到底有没有什么门道。很多年后，我在哈佛大学做萨根博士后的时候，

cues.en: I heard about the focal mission for the first time and I was really blown away by it. And I remember that I immediately made the connection back to my master's thesis and I realized that maybe one could use the earth as a refractive lens instead of the sun as a gravitational lens.
cues.zh: 我第一次听说了 focal 任务，真的被它震撼到了。我记得我立刻把它和我硕士论文联系了起来，我意识到也许可以用地球作为折射透镜，而不是用太阳作为引力透镜。

cues.en: But I was a postdoc back then. I mean, I did not have job security, was on a short term contract. And being a postdoc is kinda tough. You have to spit out lots of papers on reputable science.
cues.zh: 但那时候我还是个博士后。我是说，我没有工作保障，签的是短期合同。做博士后挺难的。你得在像样的科学期刊上大量发论文。

cues.en: And frankly, my main project was already risky enough. I was looking for exomoons for goodness sake. So I just didn't feel comfortable turning to this project and writing it up. I thought it was too risky to do.
cues.zh: 说实话，我自己的主要项目已经够冒险了。我可是在找系外卫星啊。所以我就是不太敢转向这个项目并把它写出来。我觉得做这个风险太大。

cues.en: But I told myself
cues.zh: 但我告诉自己

cues.en: as before,
cues.zh: 和之前一样，

cues.en: one day I'll come back to this. One day when I have a faculty job, I'll turn back to this and try and crack this problem. Well, last summer I realized that I'd been at Columbia as a faculty member for a couple of years now and really I could afford to finally revisit this problem,
cues.zh: 总有一天我会回来做这个。等有一天我拿到教职，我就会回过头来试着攻克这个问题。去年夏天，我意识到自己在哥伦比亚大学做教职已经好几年了，我真的可以负担得起重新审视这个问题了，

cues.en: to take a risk. And so for the last twelve months, I've been working diligently on this problem, trying to figure out if this crazy idea from my youth had any merit to it. And so thirteen years in the making, I'm delighted to say that my paper on this subject has now been accepted for publication in a peer reviewed journal.
cues.zh: 去冒这个险。所以在过去十二个月里，我一直在勤奋地研究这个问题，试图弄清楚我年轻时的这个疯狂想法到底有没有可取之处。历经十三年，我很高兴地说，我关于这个主题的论文现在已经被一本同行评审期刊接收发表了。

cues.en: And as regular subscribers of the channel will know, I'm fond of giving my projects punchy names, and so I'm delighted to introduce you today to the telescope.
cues.zh: 频道的常规订阅者都知道，我喜欢给项目起些响亮的名字，所以今天我很高兴向大家介绍 telescope。

cues.en: Imagine a distant star
cues.zh: 想象一颗遥远的恒星

cues.en: setting on the horizon.
cues.zh: 正落到地平线上。

cues.en: Light from that star enters the Earth's atmosphere and deflects by half a degree. It skims the surface and makes its way back out of the atmosphere giving another half a degree bend.
cues.zh: 来自那颗恒星的光进入地球大气层，偏折半度。它掠过地表，再穿出大气层时又偏折半度。

cues.en: So one degree in total.
cues.zh: 所以总共是一度。

cues.en: Light from that same star
cues.zh: 同一颗恒星的光

cues.en: will also shine upon the opposite hemisphere and the two rays
cues.zh: 也会照到另一个半球，而这两条光线

cues.en: will converge together at a distance given by the radius of the earth divided by one degree.
cues.zh: 会在距离等于地球半径除以一度的位置汇聚。

cues.en: So that's a distance just interior to the orbit of the moon.
cues.zh: 所以这个距离刚好在月球轨道以内。

cues.en: This is a focus point.
cues.zh: 这是一个焦点。

cues.en: If the ray were any closer to the Earth, it would strike the surface and thus be lost.
cues.zh: 如果光线离地球再近一点，就会打到地表，从而丢失。

cues.en: If the ray were a bit higher in altitude,
cues.zh: 如果光线高度再高一点，

cues.en: then it would bend a little bit less since the atmosphere is thinner as altitude increases.
cues.zh: 它偏折得就会少一点，因为高度越高大气越稀薄。

cues.en: So this means that not only do you get a focus for surface
cues.zh: 这意味着你不仅能得到掠地表

cues.en: skimming rays,
cues.zh: 光线的焦点，

cues.en: you will also get a focus at every point more distant than that too.
cues.zh: 还会在比那更远的每个点上都得到焦点。

cues.en: In other words, you have a focal line.
cues.zh: 换句话说，你得到了一条焦线。

cues.en: Now, immediate problem with this is that a ray traveling so close to the surface will surely be lost along the way. It might intercept clouds or mountains or even buildings
cues.zh: 现在，直接的问题是，如此贴近地表行进的光线肯定会在途中丢失。它可能撞上云、山甚至建筑

cues.en: or frankly even just be absorbed by the very thick atmosphere through which it has traversed.
cues.zh: 或者坦白说，甚至只是被它穿过的非常厚的大气吸收掉。

cues.en: And so it's fairly straightforward to convince yourself
cues.zh: 所以很容易说服自己

cues.en: that a surface
cues.zh: 一个表面

cues.en: skimming telescope
cues.zh: 略读望远镜

cues.en: is not going to work. So let's consider higher altitude rays.
cues.zh: 行不通。所以我们来考虑更高空的射线。

cues.en: A ray with an altitude of about a kilometer
cues.zh: 一束高度约为一公里的射线

cues.en: will focus onto the surface of the moon which would obviously be a very interesting place to put a telescope
cues.zh: 将聚焦于月球表面，这显然是一个放置望远镜的极佳地点

cues.en: but sadly scattering and extinction effects at one kilometer altitude
cues.zh: 但遗憾的是，一公里高度处的散射和消光效应

cues.en: are still rather severe.
cues.zh: 仍然相当严重。

cues.en: Extinction is very dependent on the color or wavelength of light that you're looking at. So here you can see the amplification
cues.zh: 消光非常依赖于你所观测的光的颜色或波长。所以这里你可以看到放大效果

cues.en: of the telescope assuming a one meter detector
cues.zh: 对于假设使用一米探测器的望远镜而言

cues.en: as a function of the wavelength.
cues.zh: 作为波长的函数。

cues.en: Those different colored lines correspond to different climatic conditions on Earth but they all show rather flat responses
cues.zh: 那些不同颜色的线对应地球上不同的气候条件，但它们都显示出相当平缓的响应。

cues.en: except in the gray banded regions.
cues.zh: 除了灰色带状区域之外。

cues.en: Those regions are known as atmospheric
cues.zh: 这些区域被称为大气

cues.en: windows where the Earth's atmosphere gives us a bit of a break and stops being so opaque.
cues.zh: 地球大气层为我们提供了一点喘息的机会，不再那么不透明的窗口。

cues.en: So a near infrared detector on the moon could perhaps achieve amplifications
cues.zh: 所以，月球上的近红外探测器或许能实现放大。

cues.en: of around 10 to 40,000
cues.zh: 大约在 1 万到 4 万之间

cues.en: according to my calculations.
cues.zh: 根据我的计算。

cues.en: Now all of this sounds very promising, but I haven't talked about clouds yet. Clouds cover three quarters of the Earth and can block out almost all of the light that we're trying to use in our telescope.
cues.zh: 这一切听起来很有前景，但我还没提到云。云覆盖了地球四分之三的面积，几乎能挡住我们望远镜想要利用的所有光线。

cues.en: So if we want the telescope to work, then we're gonna have to use rays which actually travel above the clouds themselves.
cues.zh: 所以如果我们想让望远镜工作，我们就得使用那些能够穿梭于云层之上的光线。

cues.en: But how high can we really go?
cues.zh: 但海拔最高能到多少？

cues.en: Because the higher in altitude we go, the less atmosphere there is, the less refraction we have, and thus the focus point moves out to potentially an unusable distance. In my paper, I suggest a realistic useful distance for lensing is the region of stable orbits around the Earth known as the Hill Sphere. By placing a detector here some four times further out than the moon's distance,
cues.zh: 因为海拔越高，大气越少，折射也越少，因此焦点会外移到可能无法使用的距离。在我的论文中，我认为透镜观测现实可用的距离，是地球周围稳定轨道区域，也就是希尔球。把探测器放在这里，比月球距离远约四倍，

cues.en: lens rays would have skimmed the earth at an altitude of 14 kilometers.
cues.zh: 透镜光线会以14公里的高度掠过地球。

cues.en: That's enough to have missed the vast majority of clouds.
cues.zh: 这足以错过绝大多数云层。

cues.en: Using high resolution cloud maps from satellite reconnaissance,
cues.zh: 利用卫星侦察获得的高分辨率云图，

cues.en: I estimate that clouds would lead to a loss of 8% of starlight in this configuration.
cues.zh: 我估计在这种配置下，云层会导致8%的星光损失。

cues.en: That's small enough that clouds no longer ruin the telescope concept. Moreover, extinction effects also dramatically drop and now you can see that most of the infrared spectrum becomes usable for lensing.
cues.zh: 这已经足够小，云层不再会毁掉望远镜构想。此外，消光效应也大幅下降，现在你可以看到，大部分红外光谱都能用于透镜观测。

cues.en: So our destination is just one hill radius away from us, which is actually the separation that many of our new space telescopes are going to, such as the upcoming James Webb Space Telescope.
cues.zh: 所以我们的目的地离我们只有一个希尔半径，而这实际上正是许多新太空望远镜将要前往的间距，比如即将发射的 James Webb Space Telescope。

cues.en: Once out here, we'd want to block out the disk of the Earth and probably the lower 14 kilometers of nonusable
cues.zh: 一旦到了那里，我们会想挡住地球圆面，可能还有低层14公里不可用的

cues.en: atmosphere too in order to reduce airglow from the lower
cues.zh: 大气，以减少来自低层的气辉

cues.en: Now whenever a star, a planet, an asteroid passes behind the earth, we will get a chance to see its light
cues.zh: 现在，每当恒星、行星或小行星从地球背后经过，我们就有机会看到它的光

cues.en: lens around the earth and that lensing should last for about a day giving amplifications
cues.zh: 绕地球形成透镜效应，而这种透镜效应应持续约一天，产生放大

cues.en: on axis
cues.zh: 轴向

cues.en: In the paper, I conservatively halved that number to account for possible losses as one side of the earth is in sunlight.
cues.zh: 在论文中，我保守地将这个数字减半，以考虑地球一侧处于阳光照射下可能造成的损失。

cues.en: So that gives you 22,500
cues.zh: 这样你就得到了 22,500

cues.en: for your amplification.
cues.zh: 为了给你放大信号。

cues.en: That's a little bit of a difficult number to pass, what that really means. So another way of thinking about it is that it's turning your one meter detector
cues.zh: 这个数字不太容易直接理解，它到底意味着什么。换个角度想，就是它把你的单米探测器

cues.en: into a telescope with the effective collecting power of a 150
cues.zh: 变成一台有效集光能力相当于150的望远镜

cues.en: meter telescope.
cues.zh: 米勒望远镜。

cues.en: So that would mean that you're moving from say tens of parts per million photometry
cues.zh:
这意味着你将从大约每百万分之几十的光度测量
@@^

cues.en: to a few parts per billion photometry.
cues.zh: 达到十亿分之几的测光精度。

cues.en: The kind of level where you can start to detect exotopography,
cues.zh: 这种层面，你已经开始能检测异位地形了，

cues.en: biosignatures,
cues.zh: 生物特征标志物，

cues.en: and very faint sources on the other side of the universe.
cues.zh: 以及宇宙另一端极其微弱的源。

cues.en: meter space based telescope
cues.zh: 基于米波空间望远镜

cues.en: would cost a ridiculous
cues.zh: 代价会极其高昂

cues.en: amount of money to build.
cues.zh: 构建所需的资金量。

cues.en: For example, the 6.5
meter James Webb Space Telescope costs about $10,000,000,000,
cues.zh: 詹姆斯·韦布空间望远镜造价约 100 亿美元，

cues.en: but a one meter detector
cues.zh: 但一米长的探测器

cues.en: using the telescope effect could cheat its way to a 150 meters achieving the same power
cues.zh: 利用望远镜效应，可以“作弊”般地达到150米，同时实现相同的功率。

cues.en: at a tiny fraction of the cost.
cues.zh: 成本微乎其微。

cues.en: Now there's no such thing as a free lunch and so there are definitely some limitations with this telescope idea. Don't get me wrong, One of the biggest limitations is that you can only look at whatever happens to be behind the earth,
cues.zh: 天下没有免费的午餐，所以这个望远镜的想法肯定有一些局限。别误会，最大的局限之一是，你只能观察恰好位于地球背后的东西。

cues.en: but the alignment doesn't have to be exact. Actually, it could be offset by about an earth diameter
cues.zh: 但对齐不必精确。实际上，它可以偏移大约一个地球直径

cues.en: and you still get plenty of lensing. You can see here an animation I made of how the lensed ring of light appears
cues.zh:
你仍然能看到大量的引力透镜效应。你可以在这里看到我制作的一个动画，展示了被透镜化的光环是如何呈现的

cues.en: as a star passes behind the earth. You actually get even higher amplifications

当恒星从地球背后经过时，你实际上会得到更高的放大率

cues.en: and that's due to the large oval shaped rim that forms at those times.
cues.zh: 这是因为在那些时间段会形成一个大型的卵形边缘。

cues.en: One could imagine using a fleet of small detectors around the Hill sphere of the Earth to enable pointing control across the sky.
cues.zh: 可以想象在地球希尔球周围部署一群小型探测器，实现全天区的指向控制。

cues.en: So all in all, I'm very excited about the prospect of a telescope system and one can even imagine trying to use this on other planets too such as Jupiter and having a JovaScope.
cues.zh: 总的来说，我对望远镜系统的前景非常兴奋，甚至可以想象在木星等其他行星上也尝试使用它，造一台“木星镜”。

cues.en: But there are plenty of things to be figured out before we could ever go and build one of these things. For instance, what is the real world performance of this system when you have atmospheric turbulence and shear effects within the atmosphere?
cues.zh: 但在真正动手建造之前，还有大量问题需要弄清楚。比如，当存在大气湍流和大气剪切效应时，这个系统在真实世界中的性能如何？

cues.en: How easily can you distinguish the lensed photons
cues.zh: 你有多容易区分被引力透镜的光子

cues.en: from the background contaminant sources in your image?
cues.zh: 和图像中的背景污染源？

cues.en: And what kind of acculta do you need to precisely remove
cues.zh: 以及你需要什么样的日冕仪来精确去除

cues.en: light from the earth? Those concerns and more that you can think of, I'm sure, are all very valid reasons to have some degree of skepticism when you think about this telescope system. And so I'm not gonna sit here and tell you that this is some kind of silver bullet to astronomy or something.
cues.zh: 来自地球的光？这些担忧，以及你肯定还能想到的更多问题，都是你在考虑这个望远镜系统时保持一定程度怀疑的充分理由。所以我不会坐在这里告诉你，这是天文学的某种灵丹妙药之类的东西。

cues.en: But,
cues.zh: 但是，

cues.en: hopefully, I've convinced you that this is an exciting enough concept that it deserves our research attention.
cues.zh: 希望我已经让你相信，这是一个足够令人兴奋的概念，值得我们投入研究关注。

cues.en: And if my paper succeeds in doing that,
cues.zh: 如果我的论文成功做到了这一点，

cues.en: then I would consider it to be a success.
cues.zh: 那我就认为它是成功的。

cues.en: Let me just finish by adding a personal note.
cues.zh: 最后让我加一句个人感言。

cues.en: This project was thirteen
cues.zh: 这个项目对我而言历时十三

cues.en: years in the making for me and that's a time scale which is long enough that this was in grave jeopardy of never coming to fruition.
cues.zh: 年才做成，这个时间尺度长到它一度岌岌可危，差点永远无法实现。

cues.en: And I bet many of you could probably relate to that feeling of having had some idea or dream from your youth
cues.zh: 我敢打赌，你们很多人都能体会那种感觉——年轻时曾有过某个想法或梦想

cues.en: that bit by bit piece by piece was dismantled
cues.zh: 却一点一点、一块一块地被瓦解了

cues.en: was
cues.zh: 被

cues.en: relegated to the wasteland of lost ambitions.
cues.zh: 贬到了失落抱负的荒原里。

cues.en: And you tell yourself that one day you'll come back to it, one day you'll pick it up and dust off that dream,
cues.zh: 你告诉自己，总有一天你会回来找它，总有一天你会重新拾起那个梦想，掸去上面的灰尘，

cues.en: but it slips
cues.zh: 但它就这样溜走了

cues.en: week after week, month after month,
cues.zh: 一周又一周，一月又一月，

cues.en: year after year.
cues.zh: 一年又一年。

cues.en: I am so privileged,
cues.zh: 我太幸运了，

cues.en: so privileged to have had the intellectual space, the job security,
cues.zh: 太幸运能拥有这样的思维空间、工作保障、

cues.en: the financial freedom to have taken a risk like this.
cues.zh: 以及财务自由，去冒这样的险。

cues.en: I could afford to put the regular bread on the table work to the side in order to focus on this project and it means a great deal to me to finish what I started all those years ago.
cues.zh: 我有能力把养家糊口的工作放到一边，专注于这个项目，能完成我多年前开始的事情，这对我意义重大。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.zh: 我得说，我有一个很大的遗憾，那就是我没有早点做这件事，

cues.zh: 听着，如果你有一个梦想、一份热情或一个想法，

cues.zh: 别像我那样。别等十五年才去追求它。我很后悔。我是说，我可能都没那么多时间了。
